result.title: Identity World Model: Recognizing People in an Imagined Latent World
result.summary: Whole-body human recognition has advanced rapidly with large vision models. However, existing methods remain fragile under real-world variations, as they tie identity to transient cues such as clothing, texture, pose, or viewpoint. We argue that a robust recognizer should not merely learn to ignore these cues, but imagine how a person would be represented if they changed. To this end, we propose IDWorld, an identity world model: just as a latent world model predicts the features of a scene after an action, IDWorld predicts how a person would be represented under a changed condition. In a single forward pass, IDWorld imagines these counterfactual features under shared canonical conditions, such as the same outfit, a fixed view, or a bare silhouette, without rendering any pixels. Compared with explicit imagination in pixels, this latent imagination keeps nearly the same accuracy while being over 11x faster, at 5.9 ms per frame. Since each imagined condition has its own strengths, IDWorld then fuses them adaptively, weighting each condition for every probe-gallery pair. Extensive experiments show that IDWorld achieves state-of-the-art results on CCPG and CCGR-MINI, outperforms the compared methods on MEVID, and generalizes best to CASIA-B* and SUSTech1K, with the best mAP on CCVID. These results suggest identity world models offer a simple yet effective path to robust recognition. Code will be released.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 IDWorld 身份世界模型：用单次前向在共享规范条件（同一服装、固定视角、裸轮廓等）下预测人物的反事实 latent 特征，不渲染像素，并对各条件的想象结果按 probe-gallery 对自适应加权融合，用于全身人物识别，在多个基准上取得领先。
AI.relevance_reason: 反事实 latent 特征预测加按样本对自适应加权，与「内部状态是否保留任务必要视觉信息、如何抑制外观旁路」有方法学线索，可供核查其作为 latent 状态不变性训练的借鉴价值，但该文属识别任务，不涉及推理生成。
